author: Mike Mahoney
title: 'You were on alert all the time': Kansas Marine reflects on Vietnam - NewsBreak
text: WICHITA, Kan. (KSNW) — Dodge City native Jesse Ramos answered the call to service in 1968 by joining the Marines. “I really did like the Marine Corps uniforms, but I think maybe once I got to ‘Nam, I had a little bit of a different tune about it,” Ramos said. After completing his training, Jesse soon found himself in Da Nang serving in the Marine Corps Infantry. His 12 months in Vietnam were spent patrolling the jungle, protecting American artillery, and constantly fighting for his life. “You were on alert all the time. You had to keep your eyes open. You just had to watch out for booby traps, anything when you were walking through the jungle. You just never knew what could come up,” Ramos said. He did his best to stay on his toes but eventually got injured when a tank he was riding struck a land mine. “It blew me up in the air, probably ten or twenty feet up in the air, but the person who was sitting right in front of me, it pulled his legs down and he lost a leg,” Ramos said. Ramos received a Purple Heart for that injury and for injuries he got during a firefight with the Vietcong. But when he looks back on his time in Vietnam, he can’t help but remember the ultimate sacrifice two of his teammates made. “Two buddies of mine hit a booby trap and it killed them. So, that was just another time that I thought, ‘It wasn’t my time to go,'” he said. Ramos has been shaken by the horrors of war but found peace through talking to others, and he encourages his fellow veterans to do the same. “If a veteran is having a lot of problems, seek help,” he said. “Don’t let it go because sometimes it will only get worse.” Jesse came back to Kansas after his year in Vietnam and was honorably discharged as an E4 corporal in 1970. He returned to the Marines in 1975 and served for another two years managing companies’ pay accounts. He later went on to have a fulfilling career as a postal worker that ended with him in the role of postmaster, and he’s now enjoying retirement with his wife in the Air Capital.
